episode_title: How AI Is Changing Engineering Teams and Hiring

real_qa.q: What skills are becoming most valuable for software engineers in the age of AI-driven code generation?
real_qa.r: Asking the right questions has become amplified in the agentic world because AI is an inference engine that does what you ask it to do. Judgment about whether you are doing the right thing and whether a solution is correct before prompting AI is becoming very important. Other critical skills include thinking from first principles, problem-solving, ideation, the ability to verify if AI outputs are correct, understanding how code impacts systems, systems engineering, architecture, and cost efficiency with AI resources.
real_qa.requete: valuable engineer skills AI code generation

real_qa.q: How has Hero Safety's engineering interview process changed to account for AI tool usage by candidates?
real_qa.r: There has been a radical shift in the last 12 months where the bug has become a feature—if you are not using AI during interviews, then it is a problem because that is what engineers will be doing on a day-to-day basis. Interviewers now extract different signals than before: candidates are evaluated for their ability to use the right AI tools and systems to code, problem-solving skills, system design, architectural skills, and first principles thinking, rather than knowledge of specific programming languages like Java or C++.

guest.bio_context: Bali Raghavan is co-founder and CTO at Hero Safety, building an end-to-end AI-enabled operating system for public safety. He has prior experience as an engineering leader and worked at Amazon, where he was involved in launching the jewelry store and TV store online.

real_quote: In the world of AI, everything is changing. The entire team is our engineering team because everyone is coding.
key_stats: 12 months: radical shift in engineering interview processes due to AI adoption
Last 24 months: significant decrease in core engineering bandwidth needed for non-critical tasks because people can take things to the finish line without engineering help
